opening.argument: The presentation identifies itself as an introduction to the central nervous system and proceeds as an instructional neuroanatomy lesson. Its narration explains that the brain has functional and anatomical regions and establishes terminology for describing them, while also teaching the planes in which a brain can be sectioned and their relevance to brain imaging. The visual material supports that instruction: a preserved brain section is labeled “MIDBRAIN” as gloved hands indicate the region. This is educational content demonstrating anatomical structures and concepts, not a proposition tied to payment, credential collection, or another apparent scam mechanism. The supplied material therefore supports an instructional purpose without establishing a transaction, promised reward, or other harmful outcome.

citations.quote: Introduction to the Central Nervous System - UBC Neuroanatomy Season 1 - Ep 1
The brain can be divided into functional and anatomical regions. We will now start with an anatomical overview to establish a common terminology and to describe the areas of the brain.
Let's look at the various planes a brain can be sectioned in. This is a very important concept because imaging of the brain uses these planes.
